text:
**Short answer:** about 300 W of solar refills a 1,000 Wh power station from empty in one good sunny day. 200 W is the common budget choice and takes about a day and a half.

**How it works**

Daily energy is roughly panel watts × peak sun hours × 0.7-0.75, because panels rarely deliver their rated output ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

| Panel size | Daily energy (4.5 sun hours, 70%) | Time to fill 1,000 Wh |
|---|---|---|
| 100 W | ~315 Wh | ~3 days |
| 200 W | ~630 Wh | ~1.5 days |
| 400 W | ~1,260 Wh | under 1 day |

Source: [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)

**Panel watts for a full recharge in one day** ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)):
- 4 peak sun hours: ~340 W
- 5 peak sun hours: ~270 W
- 6 peak sun hours: ~230 W

Winter is much worse. In a northern January with about 2 peak sun hours, you'd need roughly 700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Check before buying**
- **Station's max solar input (watts):** panels above that limit add nothing. Many 1,000 Wh stations accept 400-800 W, but some cap at 200 W.
- **Input voltage window:** the panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside it. Exceeding it can damage the station.
- **Connector:** MC4 panel connectors often need an adapter for XT60 or DC barrel ports.
- **Running loads while charging:** this slows the net recharge.
